title: Day 6 — The Concurrency Race
prompt: We have a cache that lazily builds one client per tenant. Single-threaded it's fine, but under load we sometimes build the same tenant's client more than once and hand out different objects. Here's the class — take a look and tell me what you'd do.

clarifications.answer: Yes — many threads can call get() with the same key at the same instant. Assume a real thread pool.
There's a self._lock already declared. Whether and how you use it is the whole question.
It's threads, not asyncio — plain synchronous get() called from multiple threads.
The factory is expensive and may open connections, so calling it more than once per key is the actual harm. It must run at most once per key.
Correctness first. A single lock is acceptable; if you want to avoid serializing all keys you can, but it's not required to pass.
Right — every concurrent caller for a key must get the exact same object back.

hints: Look at the two lines in get(): the 'if key not in self._store' check and the assignment. What can another thread do between them?
Two threads can both pass the 'not in' check before either assigns — so both call the factory. That's a check-then-act race.
Wrap the check-and-build in 'with self._lock:'. For bonus points, use double-checked locking so the fast path (already cached) doesn't take the lock.
